text: A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.
With my voice I cry out to the LORD; with my voice I plead with the LORD for mercy.
I pour out my complaint before him; before him I tell my trouble.
When my spirit grows faint within me, you know my path. On the road where I walk they have hidden a trap for me.
Look to my right and see: no one recognizes me. Refuge has perished from me; no one cares for my life.

versions.text: Look to my right and see: no one recognizes me. Every refuge is gone from me; no one cares for my life.
versions.explanation: 'Every refuge' adds a quantifier not present in the Hebrew, which simply says 'refuge has perished from me.' The revised line stays closer to the source while keeping the parallel rhythm of the verse.

text: I cry out to you, LORD; I say, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."
Listen to my cry, for I am brought very low. Rescue me from those who pursue me, for they are too strong for me.
Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name. The righteous will gather around me, for you will deal bountifully with me.

versions.text: Bring me out of prison, that I may praise your name. The righteous will gather around me, for you will deal bountifully with me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb להודות means 'to give thanks/acknowledge' rather than the more general 'praise' (which usually renders הלל), and נַפְשִׁי ('my soul/my life') is left untranslated. The suggested wording is closer to the Hebrew and still reads smoothly aloud.
